insurer_name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
rejection_reason: Pre-Existing Disease (PED) Non-Disclosure without Causal Nexus
rejection_letter_text:
Ref: CIR/CLM/REP/2024/098124
Date: 14-Aug-2024

Dear Policyholder,

Re: Claim No: CIR/2024/110945, Policy No: P/161112/01/2023/004521
Patient Name: Rajesh Sharma, Hospital: Apollo Hospital, Delhi
Ailment: Acute Appendicitis with Laparoscopic Appendectomy

With reference to your claim for reimbursement of hospitalization expenses incurred for acute appendicitis, our medical panel has thoroughly reviewed the submitted medical records. Upon perusal of the Indoor Case Papers (ICP), it is noted that the patient has a documented past medical history of Cervical Spondylosis and Lumbar Spondylitis for the past 4 years, which was not disclosed in the proposal form dated 12-Jan-2023.

As per Condition 4.1 (Non-Disclosure of Material Facts) read with Exclusion Clause Ex01 (Pre-Existing Diseases), the insured is under a strict duty of utmost good faith to declare all past ailments. Had this history been disclosed, our underwriters would have loaded the premium or excluded related complications. Therefore, the competent authority has repudiated the claim in toto.
detected_policy_clauses: Exclusion Clause Ex01 (Pre-Existing Diseases Waiting Period)
expected_regulations: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (2024), Clause 9.2 (Claims Review Committee Review)
IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024, Regulation 10
expected_precedents: Sulbha Prakash Motegaonkar v. Life Insurance Corporation of India ((2021) 13 SCC 561) - Nexus Principle
Manmohan Nanda v. United India Assurance Co. Ltd. (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 31) - Technical Repudiation Bar
expected_violations: Violation of the Causal Nexus Principle: Cervical spondylosis has no clinical or pathological correlation to acute appendicitis.
Unfair repudiation under Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(47) and deficiency of service under Section 2(11).
expected_recommendations: Issue a formal appeal to Star Health Grievance Redressal Officer (gro@starhealth.in) citing the Supreme Court Nexus judgment in Sulbha Motegaonkar.
Assert that cervical spondylosis has zero medical nexus with acute appendectomy.
If not resolved within 15 days, lodge an e-complaint on IRDAI Bima Bharosa portal and escalate to Insurance Ombudsman, Delhi.

insurer_name: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
rejection_reason: Repudiation for Non-Disclosure in a Policy Active for Over 6 Years (Moratorium Violation)
rejection_letter_text:
Ref: CLM/REP/HDF/2024/77421
Date: 02-Sep-2024

Dear Policyholder,

Re: Claim No: HDF/MED/2024/88312, Policy No: 2825 2018 9012 3400 00
Patient Name: Sunita Mehra, Hospital: Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Gurugram
Diagnosis: Single Vessel Coronary Artery Disease (PTCA Stent Implantation)

We refer to your mediclaim submitted for coronary angioplasty. On scrutiny of the clinical history recorded by the treating cardiologist, it is noted that the patient is a known case of Mild Essential Hypertension since 2017. However, in the original proposal form dated 15-May-2018, the answer to Question 12(a) ('Do you suffer from hypertension or high blood pressure?') was marked as 'NO'.

Since this material fact was suppressed at the inception of policy coverage, the contract is rendered void ab initio under Section C, Clause 2 (Material Information Non-Disclosure). Hence, we regret to inform you that the claim stands repudiated.
detected_policy_clauses: Section C, Clause 2 (Non-Disclosure of Material Facts)
expected_regulations: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (2024), Clause 5.1 (Continuous Coverage Moratorium Period - 60 Months)
Insurance Act, 1938, Section 45 (Incontestability Clause)
expected_precedents: Hari Om Agarwal v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. (2007 SCC OnLine Del 1251) - Hypertension as Lifestyle Condition & Main Purpose Rule
Manmohan Nanda v. United India Assurance Co. Ltd. ((2022) 10 SCC 170) - Duty of Disclosure & Incontestability
expected_violations: Direct statutory violation of IRDAI 60-Month Moratorium Rule: The policy has been continuously active for 6 years (2018-2024), making non-disclosure claims completely time-barred and incontestable.
Violation of Section 45 of Insurance Act, 1938.
expected_recommendations: Draft representation to HDFC ERGO GRO (gro@hdfcergo.com) invoking Clause 5.1 of IRDAI 2024 Health Master Circular establishing that the policy is > 6 years old and legally incontestable.
Demand immediate revocation of repudiation and payment of principal claim with 8.5% statutory penal interest.
Escalate to Insurance Ombudsman, Delhi (or Noida) if GRO fails to resolve within 14 days.

rejection_reason: Repudiation Solely Due to Delay in Claim Intimation (18 Days Delay Post-Emergency)
rejection_letter_text:
Ref: CHI/REJ/2024/90214
Date: 22-Jul-2024

Dear Policyholder,

Re: Claim No: 19827364, Policy No: 12093482
Patient Name: Vikram Patel, Hospital: Sterling Hospital, Ahmedabad
Treatment: Emergency Polytrauma Management (Road Traffic Accident)

We refer to the reimbursement claim documents submitted on 15-Jul-2024 in respect of emergency hospitalization from 20-Jun-2024 to 27-Jun-2024. As per Part B, Clause 3.1 of your policy terms:
'Notice of claim with full particulars must be given to the company in writing within 24 hours of hospitalization in case of emergency.'

In your case, intimation of claim was registered only on 15-Jul-2024, which entails an unexplained delay of 18 days beyond the contractual cutoff. Because of this late notice, the company was deprived of its valuable right to carry out contemporaneous physical verification. Consequently, the claim is rejected as barred by late intimation.
detected_policy_clauses: Part B, Clause 3.1 (Mandatory Claim Intimation Timelines)
Clause 5.2 (Condition Precedent to Admission of Liability)
expected_regulations: IRDAI Circular Ref: IRDA/HLTH/MISC/CIR/216/09/2011 (Delay in Claim Intimation Not to Be Used Mechanically)
IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (2024), Chapter IV
expected_precedents: Om Prakash v. Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. ((2017) 9 SCC 724) - Substance over Technicality & Explained Delay
Gurmel Singh v. Branch Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd. (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 506) - Lex Non Cogit Ad Impossibilia
expected_violations: Violation of IRDAI Circular 2011 prohibiting rejection solely on intimation delay when hospitalization is genuine.
Violation of Supreme Court ratio in Om Prakash v. Reliance General Insurance that emergency trauma justifies delayed paperwork.
expected_recommendations: Submit formal grievance to Care Health GRO (gro@careinsurance.com) enclosing copy of Emergency Admission Certificate and Medico-Legal Case (MLC) summary explaining the emergency ICU status.
Cite Supreme Court judgment Om Prakash v. Reliance General Insurance ((2017) 9 SCC 724) and IRDAI 2011 circular.
File complaint with Insurance Ombudsman, Ahmedabad if rejected.

insurer_name: The New India Assurance Company Limited
rejection_reason: Repudiation Due to Alleged Non-Submission of Hospital Indoor Case Papers (ICP)
rejection_letter_text:
Ref: NIA/DO-12/MED/2024/00341
Date: 05-Oct-2024

To: Smt. Ananya Sen
Policy No: 12050034232800000451, Claim No: 12050034241100000092
Hospital: AMRI Hospital, Kolkata
Diagnosis: Severe Dengue with Thrombocytopenia

Dear Madam,

We refer to your claim file for the hospitalization from 10-Aug-2024 to 16-Aug-2024. Vide our requirement letters dated 25-Aug-2024 and 10-Sep-2024, you were requested to furnish the complete Certified Hospital Indoor Case Papers (ICP) along with hourly nursing vital monitoring charts.

In response, you provided only the discharge summary, pathology platelet reports, and pharmacy bills, stating that the hospital administration refused to release hourly nursing records directly to the patient.

Since condition no. 5.4 mandates production of all original indoor records to establish active hospital management, the competent authority has closed your claim file as 'REPUDIATED / NO CLAIM' on account of non-submission of requisite documents.
detected_policy_clauses: Condition 5.7 (Insurer's Right to Requisition Clinical Records)
expected_regulations: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (2024), Clause 9.2 (Reasoned Decision Mandate)
IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations, 2024, Regulation 8
expected_precedents: Gurmel Singh v. Branch Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd. (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 506) - Lex Non Cogit Ad Impossibilia
M/s Modern Insulators Ltd. v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. ((2000) 2 SCC 734) - Technical Rejection Bar
expected_violations: Violation of the doctrine of impossibility (Lex Non Cogit Ad Impossibilia): Patient cannot compel private hospital to release confidential internal staff records.
Insurer failure to utilize TPA network inspection powers to collect ICP directly from hospital rather than penalizing consumer.
expected_recommendations: Send written escalation to New India Assurance GRO (gro@newindia.co.in) invoking Gurmel Singh v. National Insurance Co.
Point out that complete discharge summary, lab reports with platelet counts, and final bills prove genuine hospitalization.
Demand that insurer exercise its statutory inspection power to collect any internal hospital logs or settle within 14 days.

'The company shall not be liable to make any payment under this policy in respect of any expenses incurred by any Insured Person on treatment for mental disorder, cognitive impairment, or psychiatric illnesses.'

In view of the clear contractual exclusion of psychiatric and mental illnesses, the claim is repudiated.

insurer_name: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
rejection_reason: Repudiation of Modern Treatment / Robotic Surgery as 'Unproven / Cosmetic / High Cost'
rejection_letter_text:
Ref: ILG/CLM/2024/098712
Date: 11-Jun-2024

Dear Policyholder,

Re: Claim No: 84092104, Policy No: 4015/CHI/29019284/00/000
Patient Name: Arvind Kulkarni, Hospital: Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital, Mumbai
Procedure: Robotic-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy for Localized Prostate Carcinoma

We acknowledge your medical claim for prostate surgery. While coverage for open surgical excision is admissible under standard surgical terms, our medical claims assessor notes that the surgery was executed using robotic surgical instrumentation (Da Vinci Xi Surgical System).

As per Exclusion Clause 4.16 (Unproven / Advanced Technologies & High Cost Procedures):
'Expenses incurred on advanced robotic, robotic-arm assisted surgeries, or computer-controlled interventions are excluded unless specifically endorsed.'

Therefore, the robotic charges amounting to ₹2,85,000 are disallowed and deducted from the payable voucher.

rejection_reason: Capping Claim Under Secretly Introduced Sub-Limit During Policy Renewal
rejection_letter_text:

Date: 12-Sep-2024

Dear Policyholder (Shri Deepak Joshi),
Policy No: 0405002823P109283741, Claim No: 04050028241100000042
Hospital: Lilavati Hospital, Mumbai
Procedure: Total Knee Replacement (TKR) Left Knee

We refer to your claim for ₹3,40,000 for left total knee replacement. While the knee replacement is covered, please note that under the revised product terms notified in the latest policy schedule, Joint Replacement surgeries are subject to a maximum sub-limit cap of ₹1,50,000 per knee.

Accordingly, your claim has been approved for ₹1,50,000 as full and final settlement. The balance amount of ₹1,90,000 stands disallowed as exceeding the contractual sub-limit cap.
expected_regulations: IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024, Regulation 4
IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (2024), Clause 3.1 (Customer Information Sheet)
expected_precedents: Jacob Punnen & Anr. v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. ((2022) 3 SCC 393) - Affirmative Duty to Disclose Renewal Alterations
M/s Modern Insulators Ltd. v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. ((2000) 2 SCC 734) - Uncommunicated Terms Unenforceable
expected_violations: Violation of Supreme Court binding precedent in Jacob Punnen v. United India Insurance: Insurer failed to give specific prior written notice of the newly introduced sub-limit at renewal.
Deficiency in service under Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(11).
